//: Explicit classification for every composite index spec in migration/firestore/rules/firestore.indexes.json. Entries are keyed by index IDENTITY (collectionGroup, queryScope and the ordered field list), never by array position, so reordering or inserting a spec cannot change what any classification means. A spec with no entry here is REVIEW_REQUIRED and fails the dry-run index gate closed. classification values: HARD_REQUIRED_FOR_CORRECTNESS, REQUIRED_FOR_ACCEPTABLE_PERFORMANCE, REQUIRED_FOR_ACCEPTABLE_FREE_TIER_USAGE, COST_OPTIMIZATION, OPTIONAL, NOT_REQUIRED, REVIEW_REQUIRED. Only the hardDryRunGate entries block DRY_RUN_GO.

evidenceStates.MEASURED: Classification supported by a recorded measurement against the production corpus.
evidenceStates.REASONED_FROM_CORPUS: Classification derived from the recorded corpus size and the query's declared bound, without a production query plan.
evidenceStates.UNVERIFIED: No production measurement and no sufficient recorded reasoning. Fails closed.

classifications.rationale: The trips list is the common travel screen and pages 25 results. Enterprise executes unindexed queries, so the absence is a cost problem rather than a correctness one, but an unindexed scan of the recorded 99-trip corpus costs 117 conservative read units against 51 for the indexed page, and the cost scales with the tenant collection.
Same screen and the same 25-result page with a status filter applied; the unindexed cost is identical to the unfiltered list because the scan is what dominates.

classifications.query: FirestoreTravelDashboardRepository.listDashboardTrips: tenant, deletion state, payment-date range of the year.
classifications.rationale: Resolved from the real code path, not from resemblance. Reachability is proven: Dashboard.tsx:148 -> tripQueries.ts:82 -> FirestoreTravelDashboardRepository.listDashboardTrips, and also FirestoreTravelRepository.ts:473. The Dashboard is the application's landing screen, so this is the highest-frequency reachable query in the product. listDashboardTrips issues TWO queries in parallel (lines 73-74): a startDate range and a paymentDate range, each with the same ownerUid/businessId/isDeleted equalities and each bound at DASHBOARD_TRIPS_BOUND = 2000. There is no explicit orderBy, so Firestore's implicit ordering is the range field then __name__, which is exactly this index's field order. The startDate half is already served by the gated (ownerUid,businessId,isDeleted,startDate,__name__) index. Without this spec the paymentDate half is the only unserved half: on every dashboard load it falls back to merging the automatic single-field indexes and filtering the range, so its cost scales with the tenant's entire live trips collection instead of with the requested year. On the recorded 99-trip corpus that is ~99 documents scanned per load against ~25 for the year slice, and the ratio grows linearly with years of history per tenant. Correctness is not at stake: Firestore Enterprise executes the query unindexed, so this is not REQUIRED_FOR_CORRECTNESS. It is not LEGACY_UNREACHABLE because reachability is proven above, and not NOT_REQUIRED for the same reason. It is gated rather than left COST_OPTIMIZATION because the database is freeTier:true with billing disabled, the query sits on the landing screen, and its 2000-document bound is strictly larger than the 25-result page that justified gating the two sibling indexes. Fail-closed: the highest-frequency reachable query on a free-tier project is gated.
classifications.measurementMethod: Static reachability trace plus corpus-cardinality reasoning. A production query plan was not obtainable: Firestore Enterprise rejects the Explain API (INVALID_ARGUMENT: Explain options are not supported in RunQuery API for Enterprise edition), and a production cardinality measurement is meaningless because no customer data has been migrated yet. Evidence state is therefore REASONED_FROM_CORPUS, not MEASURED.

classifications.query: FirestoreTravelRepository.listDueInstallments: tenant, active status set, due date.
classifications.rationale: The recorded corpus holds 37 installment rows, so a full scan costs 44 conservative read units. The index reduces that but its absence does not block a dry-run that writes no customer data. Revisit as the collection grows.
